message.content: Buddhism was founded by Siddhartha Gautama—commonly known as the Buddha—who lived around the 5th–4th centuries BCE. He was born in Lumbini, which is today located in southern Nepal, and he spent most of his life in the Indian subcontinent, particularly in the regions that are now part of modern-day India (e.g., Bodh Gaya, Rajgir, Sarnath). Thus, Buddhism originated in the ancient Indian subcontinent, with its early development centered in what is now Nepal and northern India.
